newsitem.title: USA: Williams sets first deepwater natgas line.
newsitem.headline: Williams sets first deepwater natgas line.

text.p: Williams Cos Inc said Thursday it will undertake its first deepwater natural gas pipeline venture in the Green Canyon area of the Gulf of Mexico, offshore Louisiana.

The company will build a 35-mile, 10-inch natural gas gathering pipeling from the deepwater Genesis Field to a connection with the Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line, one of Williams' pipeline subsidiaries.
Genesis, located on Green Canyon Block 205, is operated by Chevron Corp, the majority owner. Exxon Corp and Petrofina SA also have interests in the field.
Williams said its Field Services unit will begin construction in the second half of 1997 and production is due to come on stream in late 1998.
It said Chevron will use floating production technology capable of handling an expected peak flow of some 72 million cubic feet of natural gas per day into Williams' gathering system.
The new pipeline will run from the Green Canyon area, at a depth of about 2,600 feet, to an interconnection with Transo in the Ship Shoal area.
Its statement included no financial details, and company officials did not immediaterly return phone calls.
